name: HydroForceEngine
description: Engine performing a coupling of the DEM with a volume-averaged 1D fluid resolution to simulate steady uniform unidirectional fluid flow. It has been developed and used to model steady uniform gravity-driven turbulent bedload transport [Maurin2015b]_ [Maurin2016]_ [Maurin2018]_, but can be also used...

attributes.name: averageDrag
attributes.description: Discretized average drag depth profile. No role in the engine, output parameter. For practical reason, it can be evaluated directly inside the engine, calling from python the averageProfile() method of the engine

attributes.name: averageDrag1
attributes.description: Discretized average drag depth profile of particles of type 1. Evaluated when

attributes.name: averageDrag2
attributes.description: Discretized average drag depth profile of particles of type 2. Evaluated when

attributes.name: bedElevation
attributes.description: Elevation of the bed above which the fluid flow is turbulent and the particles undergo turbulent velocity fluctuation.

attributes.name: channelWidth
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: Channel width for the evaluation of the fluid wall friction inside the fluid resolution.

attributes.name: compatibilityOldVersion
attributes.description: Option to make HydroForceEngine compatible with former scripts. Slow down slightly the calculation and will eventually be removed.

attributes.name: convAcc
attributes.description: Convective acceleration, depth dependent

attributes.name: convAccOption
attributes.description: To activate the convective acceleration option in order to account for a convective acceleration term inside the momentum balance.

attributes.name: deltaZ
attributes.description: Height of the discretization cell.

attributes.name: densFluid
attributes.description: Density of the fluid, by default - density of water

attributes.name: dpdx
attributes.description: pressure gradient along streamwise direction

attributes.name: dtFluct
attributes.description: Execution time step of the turbulent fluctuation model.

attributes.name: enableMultiClassAverage
attributes.description: Enables specific averaging for all the different particle size. Uses a lot of memory if using a lots of different particle size

attributes.name: expoRZ
attributes.description: Value of the Richardson-Zaki exponent, for the drag correction due to hindrance

attributes.name: fluctTime
attributes.description: Vector containing the time of life of the fluctuations associated to each particles.

attributes.name: fluidFrictionCoef
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: fitting coefficient for the fluid wall friction

attributes.name: fluidWallFriction
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: if set to true, introduce a sink term to account for the fluid friction at the wall, see [Maurin2015]_ for details. Requires to set the width of the channel. It might slow down significantly the calculation.

attributes.name: gravity
attributes.description: Gravity vector

attributes.name: ilm
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: type of mixing length resolution applied: 0: classical Prandtl mixing length, 1: Prandtl mixing length with free-surface effects, 2: Damp turbulence accounting for the presence of particles [Li1995]_, see [RevilBaudard2013]_ for more details.

attributes.name: irheolf
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: effective fluid viscosity option: 0: pure fluid viscosity, 1: Einstein viscosity.

attributes.name: iturbu
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: activate the turbulence resolution, 1, or not, 0

attributes.name: iusl
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: option to set the boundary condition at the top of the fluid, 0: Dirichlet, fixed ($u=uTop$ en $z=h$), 1:Neumann, free-surface ($du/dz=0$ en $z=h$).

attributes.name: kappa
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: Von Karman constant. Can be tuned to account for the effect of particles on the fluid turbulence, see e.g. [RevilBaudard2015]_

attributes.name: lift
attributes.description: Option to activate or not the evaluation of the lift

attributes.name: lubrication
attributes.description: Condition to activate the calculation of the lubrication force.

attributes.name: multiDragPart
attributes.description: Spatial-averaged mean drag force for each class of particle. Un-used ? Or just for debug.

attributes.name: multiPhiPart
attributes.description: Spatial-averaged solid volume fraction for each class of particle.

attributes.name: multiVxPart
attributes.description: Spatial-averaged velocity in x direction for each class of particle.

attributes.name: multiVyPart
attributes.description: Spatial-averaged velocity in y direction for each class of particle.

attributes.name: multiVzPart
attributes.description: Spatial-averaged velocity in z direction for each class of particle.

attributes.name: nCell
attributes.description: Number of cell in the depth

attributes.name: nbAverageT
attributes.description: If >0, perform a time-averaging (in addition to the spatial averaging) over nbAverage steps.

attributes.name: phiBed
attributes.description: Turbulence modelling parameter. Associated with mixing length modelling ilm = 5.

attributes.name: phiMax
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: maximum solid volume fraction.

attributes.name: phiPart
attributes.description: Discretized solid volume fraction depth profile. Can be taken as input parameter or evaluated directly inside the engine, calling from python the averageProfile() function

attributes.name: phiPart1
attributes.description: Discretized solid volume fraction depth profile of particles of type 1. Evaluated when

attributes.name: phiPart2
attributes.description: Discretized solid volume fraction depth profile of particles of type 2. Evaluated when

attributes.name: pointParticleAverage
attributes.description: Evaluate the averaged with a point particle method. If False, consider the particle extent and weigth the averaged by the volume contained in each averaging cell.

attributes.name: radiusPart
attributes.description: Reference particle radius

attributes.name: radiusPart1
attributes.description: Radius of the particles of type 1. Useful only when

attributes.description: Radius of the particles of type 2. Useful only when

attributes.name: radiusParts
attributes.description: Variables containing the number of different radius of particles in the simulation. Allow to perform class averaging by particle size.

attributes.name: roughnessPartScale
attributes.description: Roughness length scale of the particle. In practice, the lubrication force is cut off when the two particles are at a distance roughnessPartScale.

attributes.name: steadyFlow
attributes.description: Condition to modify the buoyancy force according to the physical difference between a fluid at rest and a steady fluid flow. For more details see [Maurin2018]_

attributes.name: taufsi
attributes.description: Fluid Resolution: Create Taufsi/rhof = dragTerm/(rhof(vf-vxp)) to transmit to the fluid code

attributes.name: turbulentViscosity
attributes.description: Fluid Resolution: turbulent viscocity as a function of the depth

attributes.name: twoSize
attributes.description: Not maintained anymore. Option to activate when considering two particle size in the simulation. When activated evaluate the average solid volume fraction and drag force for the two type of particles of diameter diameterPart1 and diameterPart2 independently.

attributes.name: uTop
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: fluid velocity at the top boundary when iusl = 0

attributes.name: unCorrelatedFluctuations
attributes.description: Condition to generate uncorrelated fluid fluctuations. Default case represent in free-surface flows, for which the vertical and streamwise fluid velocity fluctuations are correlated (see e.g. reference book of Nezu & Nagakawa 1992, turbulence in open channel flows).

attributes.name: vCell
attributes.description: Volume of averaging cell

attributes.name: vFluctX
attributes.description: Vector associating a streamwise fluid velocity fluctuation to each particle. Fluctuation calculated in the C++ code from the discrete random walk model

attributes.name: vFluctY
attributes.description: Vector associating a spanwise fluid velocity fluctuation to each particle. Fluctuation calculated in the C++ code from the discrete random walk model

attributes.name: vFluctZ
attributes.description: Vector associating a normal fluid velocity fluctuation to each particle. Fluctuation calculated in the C++ code from the discrete random walk model

attributes.name: vPart
attributes.description: Discretized streamwise solid velocity depth profile, in x, y and z direction. Only the x direction measurement is taken into account in the 1D fluid coupling resolution. The two other can be used as output parameters. The x component can be taken as input parameter, or evaluated directly inside the engine, calling from python the averageProfile() function

attributes.description: If true, activate the determination of turbulent fluid velocity fluctuation for the next time step only at the position of each particle, using a simple discrete random walk (DRW) model based on the Reynolds stresses profile (

attributes.name: viscoDyn
attributes.description: Dynamic viscosity of the fluid, by default - viscosity of water

attributes.name: viscousSubLayer
attributes.description: Fluid resolution: solve the viscous sublayer close to the bottom boundary if set to 1

attributes.name: vxFluid
attributes.description: Discretized streamwise fluid velocity depth profile at t

attributes.name: vxPart
attributes.description: Discretized streamwise solid velocity depth profile. Can be taken as input parameter, or evaluated directly inside the engine, calling from python the averageProfile() function

attributes.name: vxPart1
attributes.description: Discretized solid streamwise velocity depth profile of particles of type 1. Evaluated when

attributes.name: vxPart2
attributes.description: Discretized solid streamwise velocity depth profile of particles of type 2. Evaluated when

attributes.name: vyPart
attributes.description: Discretized spanwise solid velocity depth profile. Can be taken as input parameter, or evaluated directly inside the engine, calling from python the averageProfile() function

attributes.name: vyPart1
attributes.description: Discretized solid spanwise velocity depth profile of particles of type 1. Evaluated when

attributes.name: vyPart2
attributes.description: Discretized solid spanwise velocity depth profile of particles of type 2. Evaluated when

attributes.name: vzPart
attributes.description: Discretized wall-normal solid velocity depth profile. Can be taken as input parameter, or evaluated directly inside the engine, calling from python the averageProfile() function

attributes.name: vzPart1
attributes.description: Discretized solid wall-normal velocity depth profile of particles of type 1. Evaluated when

attributes.name: wallFrictionModel
attributes.description: Model used to compute the wall friction factor $f$. 0: Blasius (1913) explicit formula $f=0.3164/Re^{1/4}$ (faster), 1: Graf and Altinakar (1998) implicit formula $f=(2\log_{10}(Re \sqrt{f_{old}} /4) + 0.32)^{-2}$.

attributes.name: zRef
attributes.description: Position of the reference point which correspond to the first value of the fluid velocity, i.e. to the ground.

methods.name: computeRadiusParts
methods.description: compute the different class of radius present in the simulation.

methods.name: fluidResolution
methods.description: Solve the 1D volume-averaged fluid momentum balance on the defined mesh (nCell<HydroForceEngine.nCell>, deltaZ<HydroForceEngine.deltaZ>) from the volume-averaged solid profiles (phiPart<HydroForceEngine.phiPart>,vxPart<HydroForceEngine.vxPart>,averageDrag<HydroForceEngine.averageDrag>), which can be evaluated with the averageProfile function.

methods.name: initialization
methods.description: Initialize the necessary parameters to make HydroForceEngine run. Necessary to execute before any simulation run, otherwise it crashes

methods.name: turbulentFluctuation
methods.description: Apply a discrete random walk model to the evaluation of the drag force to account for the fluid velocity turbulent fluctuations. Very simple model applying fluctuations from the values of the Reynolds stresses in order to recover the property $<u_x'u_z'> (z) = <R^f_{xz}>(z)/\rho^f$. The random fluctuations are modified over a time scale given by the eddy turn over time.

methods.name: turbulentFluctuationZDep
methods.description: Apply turbulent fluctuation to the problem similarly to turbulentFluctuation but with an update of the fluctuation depending on the particle position.
